title: Sopa de Lima
subtitle: Yucatan chicken and lime soup with fried tortilla strips
excerpt: Sopa de lima is a bright, lightly spiced chicken soup from the Yucatan Peninsula. Fresh lime juice is added at the end to keep the flavour sharp and clean. Fried tortilla strips float on top for crunch.
sourceNotes: Sopa de lima is a traditional soup from the Yucatan Peninsula. It uses lima, a type of sour orange-lime hybrid local to the region. Outside Mexico, regular limes give an excellent result. The soup is a staple at Yucatecan family tables and local restaurants.

content.text: This recipe serves 4 and takes 50 minutes in total. The chicken is poached directly in the broth with onion, garlic, tomatoes and jalapeño to build flavour, then shredded and returned to the soup. The lime juice goes in right at the end so the citrus stays fresh rather than cooking down to something flat.

Fry the tortilla strips in hot oil until golden and crisp just before serving. Do not add them too early or they will go soft. Cut the tortillas into thin strips, no more than 1cm wide, so they stay crunchy in the bowl. Season them lightly with salt while still hot from the oil.

items.prepNote: cut into thin strips and fried

content.text: Heat the vegetable oil in a large saucepan over a medium hob. Add the diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute.
Add the diced tomatoes and the whole jalapeño to the pan. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the tomatoes begin to break down.

Add the bone-in chicken thighs and pour in 1.2 litres of cold water. Season generously with salt. Bring to the boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.

While the soup simmers, cut the corn tortillas into strips no more than 1cm wide. Heat a thin layer of oil in a frying pan over a high hob and fry the strips in batches for 1 to 2 minutes until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper and season with salt.
Remove the chicken thighs from the broth. Pull the meat from the bones with two forks and shred it roughly. Discard the bones and the jalapeño.
Return the shredded chicken to the broth. Stir in the lime juice. Taste and adjust the seasoning. The soup should be sharp and bright.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Scatter the fried tortilla strips over the top and finish with fresh coriander leaves. Serve immediately.

attrs.symptom: The soup tastes flat despite plenty of lime
attrs.cause: The lime was added too early and the citrus cooked away during simmering
attrs.fix: Add lime juice only after the heat is off or just before ladling. Lime loses its brightness quickly at high temperatures. If the soup still tastes flat, add another squeeze of fresh lime at the table.

attrs.symptom: The chicken is dry and stringy
attrs.cause: The thighs were overcooked at too high a simmer
attrs.fix: Keep the heat at a gentle simmer, not a rolling boil. Check the chicken at 20 minutes. It is done when the juices run clear and the meat pulls easily from the bone. Remove it promptly and do not leave it sitting in the hot broth.

attrs.symptom: The tortilla strips go soft in the bowl before the soup is eaten
attrs.cause: The strips were added too early or were not fried crisp enough
attrs.fix: Fry the strips until fully golden and crisp, not just lightly coloured. Add them right at the moment of serving, or pass them at the table so each person adds their own. Keeping them separate preserves the crunch.

content.text: Sopa de lima belongs to the Yucatan Peninsula in south-eastern Mexico. The region has its own food traditions, separate from the rest of the country. This soup is on the menu at nearly every local restaurant and in most family homes. The combination of chicken, lime and fried tortilla is simple but distinctive.
